verses.text: Theophilus, in my first book I wrote about everything Jesus began to do and teach
until the day he was taken up to heaven. Before that, through the Holy Spirit, he gave instructions to the apostles he had chosen.
After he suffered, he showed them in many convincing ways that he was alive. Over forty days he appeared to them and spoke about God’s Kingdom.
While he was gathered with them, he told them, “Don’t leave Jerusalem. Wait for what the Father promised—the promise you heard me talk about.
“John baptized with water, but in just a few days you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.”
When they met together, they asked him, “Lord, are you going to restore the kingdom to Israel now?”
He replied, “You don’t need to know the dates or times the Father has set by his own authority.
“But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you. You will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, throughout Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.”
After saying this, he was lifted up as they watched, and a cloud took him out of their sight.
They kept staring into the sky as he went. Suddenly, two men dressed in white stood beside them
and said, “Men of Galilee, why are you standing here looking into the sky? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you saw him go.”
Then they returned to Jerusalem from the hill called Olivet, which is near the city, about a Sabbath day’s walk away.

When they arrived, they went upstairs to the room where they were staying. Those there were Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.
They all kept meeting together in prayer, along with the women, Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brothers.
During those days, Peter stood up among the believers—about 120 people were gathered—and said,
“Brothers and sisters, Scripture had to be fulfilled. The Holy Spirit spoke through David about Judas, who led the people who arrested Jesus.
“He was counted as one of us and shared in this ministry.”
“With the money he got for his wickedness, Judas bought a field. He fell headfirst, his body split open, and his insides spilled out.
“Everyone living in Jerusalem heard about it, so in their language they called that field Akeldama, meaning ‘Field of Blood.’
“The Psalms say, ‘Let his home become deserted; let no one live there,’ and, ‘Let someone else take his position.’
“So we need to choose one of the men who accompanied us the whole time the Lord Jesus lived among us,
“from the time John baptized people until the day Jesus was taken up from us. One of them must join us as a witness to his resurrection.”
They put forward two men: Joseph called Barsabbas, also known as Justus, and Matthias.
They prayed, “Lord, you know everyone’s heart. Show us which of these two you have chosen
“to take this ministry and apostleship that Judas left to go where he belongs.”
Then they cast lots, and the lot chose Matthias. He was added to the eleven apostles.
